evidence.positive: Against the running app (localhost:62189, image guidedclinical/orci:loop-e7eeafd6c) I seeded a mayo-mayo case by injecting the repo's real SIU^S14 in-room fixture via POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send (X-Tenant-Id: mayo-mayo), giving patient pmrn 99677001 and case OR2677CASE1, then set operations.start_time='2026-06-16 12:00:00' with end_time NULL so glucose results fall inside the case window. Injecting a Mayo flowsheet ORU^R01 with OBX 14032053^Glucose^MA451 = 142 at 20260616185000 produced, with no exception: 'Applied 1 HL7-sourced observations: 1 inserted/corrected, 0 deleted' then 'Handling event EventCategoryEvent(sourceEventType=ORU_GLUCOSE, patientId=PatientId[value=99677001], caseId=CaseId[value=OR2677CASE1], eventCategories=[GLUCOSE_UPDATED], eventDate=Tue Jun 16 23:50:00 UTC 2026...)' and the downstream glucose rules ran ('Rule evaluated: a-hypoglycemia -> false', 'Glucose value 142.0 is not below 70.0 mg/dL ... skip scheduling a-hypoglycemia-glucose-check-15min'). The event committed: mayo-mayo.operation_events gained event_category=GLUCOSE_UPDATED, source_event_type=ORU_GLUCOSE, timestamp=2026-06-16 23:50:00, alongside the persisted patient_observations row (GLUCOSE, code 14032053, value 142). A follow-up ORU carrying two glucose results on distinct OBX-4 sub-ids (205 and 198) dispatched and persisted both GLUCOSE_UPDATED rows (2026-06-17 00:20:00 and 00:25:00), so the whole per-result loop completes. Final state: 7 GLUCOSE_UPDATED rows, zero 'No active transaction' occurrences while the shipped classes were in place.
evidence.negative: Injected a glucose ORU for the same patient whose effective time falls outside the case window (20260616050000 -> 2026-06-16 10:00 UTC, before the 12:00 start_time), value 88. The app logged 'No operation for glucose observation at Tue Jun 16 10:00:00 UTC 2026 - patient PatientId[value=99677001]; skipping glucose-driven rules' followed by 'Applied 1 HL7-sourced observations: 1 inserted/corrected, 0 deleted' - no 'Handling event' line, no exception, no HL7 processor failure. mayo-mayo.operation_events stayed at its prior count of 1 while mayo-mayo.patient_observations gained the GLUCOSE 88 @ 2026-06-16 10:00:00 row, so the absence of a GLUCOSE_UPDATED event is a real skip decision and provably not a dropped or unprocessed message.
evidence.red_check: Ran pre-fix code in the container. Took the shipped source of DefaultHL7ProcessingContext.java and reverted exactly the fix's saveObservations hunk back to its parent-commit (7f500b7d6) form - 'eventService.handleEvent(buildGlucoseUpdatedEvent(...)); scheduleHypoglycemiaRecheck(...);' with no try/catch - leaving every other member identical to HEAD so nothing else in the running app broke. Compiled it inside the container with javac against /app/classes plus /app/libs/*.jar, using a copied-in lombok 1.18.46 jar purely as the annotation processor (lombok is absent from the runtime classpath). javap confirmed the swap landed on the right call site: pre-fix DefaultHL7ProcessingContext$5 (the saveObservations afterCommit) references handleEvent and no longer contains the 'Failed to dispatch GLUCOSE_UPDATED' string, while the shipped $5 references handleEventInNewTransaction and does contain it. Backed up all eight shipped class files with sha1 checksums, copied the pre-fix classes into /app/classes/com/guided/orci/service/hl7/, restarted the container (booted cleanly, 'Started OrciApplication in 11.596 seconds'). Re-sending a glucose ORU for the same open case then went red exactly as Sentry reported: 'HL7 processor MayoHL7OruProcessor failed for type=ORU^R01 tenant=mayo-mayo' with 'org.springframework.dao.InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException: No active transaction' caused by 'jakarta.persistence.TransactionRequiredException: No active transaction', and a stack trace matching the ticket frame-for-frame (DefaultHL7ProcessingContext$5.afterCommit -> EventService.handleEvent -> EventService.handleEventCategoryEvent -> DefaultTransactionStatus.flush). operation_events did NOT grow - the GLUCOSE_UPDATED event was lost even though the observation row committed. Repeated the red check with a two-glucose ORU (sub-ids 1 and 2): only the first result was dispatched (and threw), the second produced no 'Handling event' line at all and both events were lost, while both observations persisted - the collateral damage the new per-result try/catch prevents. Then restored all eight shipped class files, verified every sha1 matched the backup byte-for-byte ('CHECKSUMS IDENTICAL'), removed the scratch build dir from the container, restarted, and re-ran the positive case: both glucose results dispatched again with no exception and two fresh GLUCOSE_UPDATED rows committed.

caveats: Only the glucose/ORU call site was exercised at runtime; the same fix also rerouted the cancelMedAdmin and cancelInfusionAdmin afterCommit dispatches (MedicationAdministrationCancelledEvent), which I did not inject RAS cancels for.

operations.start_time was set with SQL rather than by a real case start, because Mayo case start needs Epic FHIR calls this isolated container cannot make; the transaction boundary under test is unaffected by how start_time got there.

The new per-result try/catch guard's containment behaviour could not be observed under the fixed code, since nothing throws on the fixed path - its value was only shown indirectly, by watching the pre-fix code abort the second glucose result.
Validated on tenant mayo-mayo only (the tenant in the Sentry report); the code path is tenant-generic but MGB/demo ORU routes were not exercised.

Unrelated observation surfaced while building fixtures: two OBX rows sharing the same MA451 code and an empty OBX-4 sub-id collapse into one observation whose observation_value is the two values newline-joined ('155\n161'), which is not numerically parseable; distinct sub-ids are required to get separate observations.

automation.assessment: Coverage from the fix commit is solid for the single-glucose happy path: DefaultHL7ProcessingContextGlucoseDispatchIntegrationTest is deliberately non-transactional so the afterCommit callback actually fires and it asserts one GLUCOSE_UPDATED OperationEvent persists, and DefaultHL7ProcessingContextObservationDispatchTest verifies dispatch routes through handleEventInNewTransaction (with never() guards on the no-operation and non-glucose cases). Two gaps remain, both matching what I exercised by hand: nothing covers more than one glucose result in a single ORU, and nothing covers the new per-result try/catch - if that guard were deleted, every existing test would still pass. The two other rerouted call sites (cancelMedAdmin, cancelInfusionAdmin) have no non-transactional test asserting their afterCommit dispatch commits.
proposed_tests: Non-transactional integration test: saveObservations with two glucose observations for the same open operation persists two GLUCOSE_UPDATED OperationEvents (locks in the per-result loop completing, which the pre-fix code aborted after the first).

Supplemental test for the per-result guard: stub EventService.handleEventInNewTransaction to throw for the first glucose only, then assert the second glucose still dispatches and saveObservations does not propagate the exception.
Non-transactional integration test for cancelMedAdmin's afterCommit dispatch, asserting the MedicationAdministrationCancelledEvent handling commits rather than failing with 'No active transaction'.
Assertion in the existing glucose dispatch integration test that no InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException is logged, so a future REQUIRED regression fails loudly rather than only losing the event.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

This was validated manually against a throwaway instance built from e7eeafd6c, on tenant mayo-mayo, by injecting real HL7 through the admin send endpoint (the same processTenantMessage path as the live integration route).

Positive: a Mayo flowsheet ORU^R01 carrying glucose 142 for an open case dispatched GLUCOSE_UPDATED with no exception, the downstream glucose rules ran, and the OperationEvent row committed. A second ORU carrying two glucose results on distinct OBX sub-ids persisted both events.

Negative: a glucose result whose effective time falls before the case start logged "No operation for glucose observation ... skipping glucose-driven rules", added no OperationEvent, and still persisted the observation row - so the absence is a real skip, not a dropped message.

Red check: the pre-fix version of the saveObservations afterCommit hunk was compiled and swapped into /app/classes, and the same ORU then reproduced the reported failure exactly - "HL7 processor MayoHL7OruProcessor failed for type=ORU^R01 tenant=mayo-mayo" with InvalidDataAccessApiUsageException: No active transaction, a stack trace matching the ticket frame-for-frame, and the GLUCOSE_UPDATED event lost. With two glucose results in one message, the pre-fix code also abandoned the second result entirely, which is what the new per-result guard prevents. The shipped classes were restored, checksums verified identical, and the positive case re-ran clean.

Automation: the fix already ships a non-transactional integration test for the single-glucose dispatch. Worth adding on top - a multi-glucose dispatch test, a test that forces the first glucose dispatch to throw and asserts the second still fires, and equivalent afterCommit coverage for the medication-cancel call sites.

Caveats: only the glucose/ORU call site was exercised at runtime; the medication-cancel call sites the same fix rerouted were not. The case start time was seeded with SQL because Mayo case start requires Epic FHIR calls this instance cannot make.
